# Cursor Pricing in 2026: Every Plan, and Why Bills Surprise People

Coworker AI breaks down Cursor pricing after the Oct 12 move to The X Subscription: Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100, Ultra $200, Teams from $30/seat.

Dhruv KapadiaSeptember 19, 202628 min readUpdated October 19, 2026

On this page

**Since October 12, 2026, new Cursor customers buy it through The X Subscription:** Free, Plus at $8 a month, Premium at $30, Super at $100 and Ultra at $200, with Teams seats at $30, $100 or $200 per user per month and Enterprise on request ([Cursor pricing](https://cursor.com/pricing)). Third-party models such as Claude, GPT and Gemini are no longer included in any new plan; on Premium and above they bill at API list price from prepaid credit. Existing subscribers can keep the legacy plans: Pro $20, Pro+ $60, Ultra $200, and Teams at $40 or $120 per seat.

Last checked: October 19, 2026, against [cursor.com/pricing](https://cursor.com/pricing), Cursor's [Models & Pricing](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing), [Team Pricing](https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/pricing) and [Legacy Cursor plans](https://cursor.com/docs/account/pricing/legacy-cursor-plans) docs, and SpaceXAI's [October 12 announcement](https://x.ai/news/x-subscription).

## Cursor pricing in 2026: every plan explained

Cursor's [pricing page](https://cursor.com/pricing) and [Models & Pricing docs](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing) list five individual tiers on The X Subscription, plus Teams and Enterprise. Every tier also carries Grok and X benefits, which this post leaves aside:

| Plan | Price | What it includes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0/month | Limited Agent and Chat usage with Cursor's own models |
| Plus | $8/month | Base weekly pool for Cursor's own models at fixed settings; no Auto, Cloud Agents, Bugbot or third-party models |
| Premium | $30/month | 4x Plus usage; adds Cloud Agents, Automations, Bugbot, Origin, and third-party models at API list price from prepaid credit |
| Super | $100/month | 15x Plus usage, priority model access at peak times |
| Ultra | $200/month | 50x Plus usage, earliest access to new products and models |
| Teams | $30, $100 or $200 per seat/month | Seats match Premium, Super or Ultra; SSO, centralized billing, usage analytics; free seats for members on their own plan |
| Enterprise | Custom quote | Pooled usage across Grok and Cursor, invoicing, SCIM, audit logs, granular spend controls |

Annual billing costs $80 a year for Plus, $300 for Premium, $1,000 for Super and $2,000 for Ultra, which works out to two months free. Prices exclude tax ([Cursor help](https://cursor.com/help/account-and-billing/pricing)).

### What happened to Pro, Pro+ and Teams Standard

Cursor's previous plans are now [legacy plans](https://cursor.com/docs/account/pricing/legacy-cursor-plans). They are closed to new customers, but existing subscribers keep their plan, price and features unless they switch, and switching is permanent. Cursor maps them like this:

| Legacy plan | Price | Closest plan on The X Subscription |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hobby | Free | Free |
| Start (India only) | ₹649/month, tax inclusive | Plus ($8) |
| Pro | $20/month | Premium ($30) |
| Pro+ | $60/month | Super ($100) |
| Ultra | $200/month | Ultra ($200) |
| Teams Standard | $40/user/month | Teams Premium seat ($30) |
| Teams Premium | $120/user/month | Teams Super seat ($100) |

The trade in that mapping: SpaceXAI [says](https://x.ai/news/x-subscription) each new plan includes at least twice the coding usage with Cursor's own models as the plan it replaces, but the new plans drop the included allowance for third-party models. If most of your work runs on Claude or GPT inside Cursor, a switch moves that spend from included usage to prepaid credit at API list price. Compare both before you switch.

Comparing what enterprise AI costs? See Coworker on your own tools in a 20-minute demo.

[Book a demo](https://coworker.ai/contact)

## Why third-party models trip people up

The number that actually matters isn't the plan price, it's what happens when you leave Cursor's own models. On The X Subscription, each paid plan includes a weekly pool that covers only Cursor models (Grok 4.7, Grok 4.6, Grok 4.5 and Composer 2.5), shared with your Grok usage. Claude, GPT and Gemini are not in that pool at all: on Premium and above they bill at API list price from prepaid credit, from the first request.

Third-party spend tracks that model's underlying API rate, not a flat per-request fee. A simple syntax fix costs a fraction of a cent. An agent run that touches a large codebase on an expensive model can burn through several dollars of credit in one session. [Superblocks' breakdown of Cursor's pricing](https://www.superblocks.com/blog/cursor-enterprise) (July 2026) names the three things that drained credits fastest under the old plans: manually picking premium models instead of Auto, enabling Max Mode, and working across large codebases that feed many files into every prompt. The first and third still apply; Max Mode now exists only on legacy request-based plans.

On legacy Pro, Pro+ and Ultra the same mechanics run through a monthly Other Models pool instead of prepaid credit. Either way, that's a genuinely different mental model from a flat per-seat SaaS price, and it's the single biggest source of "why is my bill higher than I expected" complaints.

## How Cursor's usage pools work in 2026

On The X Subscription there is one weekly pool for Cursor's own models, shared across Cursor and Grok, and it refreshes every week rather than every billing cycle. Legacy plans keep two monthly pools. [Cursor's Models & Pricing](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing) and [legacy-plan](https://cursor.com/docs/account/pricing/legacy-cursor-plans) docs, checked October 19, 2026, split them like this:

*   **Weekly pool (The X Subscription).** Cursor's own models: Grok 4.7, Grok 4.6, Grok 4.5 and Composer 2.5. Usage past the pool, and every third-party request, is paid from prepaid credit through top-ups.
*   **Two monthly pools (legacy plans).** Cursor Models for the same first-party models, and Other Models for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others at each model's API rate. Pro, Pro+, Ultra and legacy Teams include both; Start and Hobby include only Cursor Models.

Which pool a request lands in decides most of your bill, because the published per-million-token rates differ by more than an order of magnitude. From that same docs page:

| Model | Input per 1M tokens | Output per 1M tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Composer 2.5 | $0.50 | $2.50 |
| Grok 4.6 | $2  | $6  |
| Claude Sonnet 5 | $2  | $10 |
| Gemini 3.1 Pro | $2  | $12 |
| GPT-5.6 Terra | $2  | $12 |

## Questions & Answers

### What is the right plan for me?↓↑

We recommend Premium for new AI users, Super for daily agent users, and Ultra for power users. Plus is recommended for social creators with limited AI usage. The Teams plan is recommended for professionals collaborating with others, and larger organizations that need invoicing, pooled usage, or advanced security should choose Enterprise.

### What are my payment options?↓↑

Self-serve plans support all major credit and debit cards. For invoice-based billing and wire transfers, please [contact us](https://cursor.com/contact-sales?source=pricing_faq) to discuss the Enterprise plan.

### How do usage limits work?↓↑

Every tier includes a pool of AI usage shared across Cursor and Grok. Within Grok, the pool covers Chat, Imagine, Voice, and Bot. Higher tiers include larger pools, and usage costs vary by product. Your allowance refreshes weekly, so one heavy day never wipes out your whole month.

By purchasing a Start plan, you agree to the [Terms](https://cursor.com/terms/pricing). The Start plan is available with monthly billing only. Individual and Teams plan pricing is estimated at current exchange rates.

## Questions & Answers

### What is the Cursor Start plan?↓↑

Cursor Start is an accessible monthly plan made for builders in India. Start adds more access to Grok and Composer models in addition to access to cloud agents, Cursor for iOS with remote control, and the ability to extend Cursor to other tools and workflows using plugins, MCP servers, hooks, and skills.

### Where is Cursor Start available?↓↑

Cursor Start is available to our users in India. Availability may expand to select regions over time.

### How is Cursor Start billed?↓↑

Start is billed monthly in INR. You can pay with UPI, credit card, or debit card. For UPI, you'll approve a monthly autopay mandate in your UPI app at checkout, and renewals happen automatically. Annual billing is not available for the Start plan.

### How do I subscribe to Cursor Start?↓↑

You can purchase or upgrade to Cursor Start from the [pricing page](https://cursor.com/pricing) or directly within Cursor in the desktop app or web. Just sign in to your account, select the Start plan, and start coding.
